summary: This standards-track memo supplements RFC 3279. It describes how to use the RSASSA-PSS signature algorithm, the RSAES-OAEP key transport algorithm, and additional hash functions in X.509 certificates and certificate revocation lists.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4055 explains how X.509 certificates describe several RSA algorithms and their settings. The rules let a certificate identify how its public key may be used and how signatures should be checked.

subtitle: How X.509 certificates identify RSA-PSS signatures, RSA-OAEP keys and SHA-2 algorithms.

tldr.problem: X.509 profiles needed identifiers and parameter rules for newer RSA signature and key-transport algorithms.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4055 defines how certificates and CRLs identify RSASSA-PSS and RSAES-OAEP keys, and adds SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 identifiers for PKCS #1 version 1.5 signatures.
tldr.outcome: Certificates can restrict an RSA key to PSS signing or OAEP key transport and specify algorithm parameters. The RFC updates RFC 3279 and is updated by RFC 5756.

sections.title: What the RFC Adds to X.509
sections.content:
RFC 4055 supplements the X.509 certificate and CRL profile in RFC 3279. It defines conventions for RSASSA-PSS signatures and RSAES-OAEP key transport, including algorithm identifiers and parameter formats.

It also adds identifiers for SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 with PKCS #1 version 1.5 signatures. The rules apply to certificate and CRL fields such as signatureAlgorithm and subjectPublicKeyInfo, and identify suitable keyUsage values.
sections.plainLanguage: A certificate needs a clear way to name the algorithm used with its RSA key. This RFC defines identifiers and settings for PSS, OAEP and additional hash functions.

sections.title: Identifying an RSA Public Key
sections.content:
The traditional rsaEncryption identifier remains available when the key owner does not restrict the key to one scheme; its parameters must be NULL. To limit a key to PSS, use id-RSASSA-PSS. To limit it to OAEP, use id-RSAES-OAEP. A key cannot be restricted to both schemes together.

In each case the public key uses the same RSAPublicKey structure containing the modulus and public exponent. A certificate's keyUsage extension describes permitted uses. A key marked for PSS or OAEP must only be used with that scheme and any parameters stated in the certificate.
sections.plainLanguage: The certificate can leave an RSA key unrestricted or label it for PSS signatures or OAEP key transport. A restricted key must be used only for the labelled purpose.

sections.title: Hash and Mask Generation Functions
sections.content:
The supported hash functions are SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. SHA-224 is added here; the others were already supported by PKCS #1 version 2.1. The only mask generation function in this specification is MGF1.

Implementations MUST support SHA-1 and MGF1 and MAY support the other listed hashes. For hash identifiers, implementations MUST accept both a NULL parameter and an absent parameter as equivalent encodings.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC lists the hash functions and the one mask-generation function that implementations may use. It also requires accepting two encodings for hash identifiers as equivalent.

sections.title: RSASSA-PSS Signature Parameters
sections.content:
PSS parameters identify a hash algorithm, a mask-generation algorithm, salt length and trailer field. The defaults are SHA-1, MGF1 with SHA-1, a salt length of 20 octets and trailer field 1, which represents 0xBC. SHA-1 implementations must accept omitted fields as the defaults.

The RFC recommends using the same hash for PSS and MGF1. A signature's parameters must match the key's parameters except for salt length; the signature salt length must be at least the key's value. Signature values in certificates and CRLs are represented as bit strings.
sections.plainLanguage: A PSS signature includes settings for its hash, mask generation, salt and trailer. When the key also lists settings, the signature must follow them, with a specific rule for salt length.

sections.title: RSAES-OAEP and Version 1.5 Signatures
sections.content:
OAEP parameters identify a hash, a mask-generation function and a source for the encoding parameter P. The defaults use SHA-1, MGF1 with SHA-1 and an empty P value. Conforming CAs and applications must support OAEP with SHA-1; other listed hashes are optional.

The RFC also defines identifiers for SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 with PKCS #1 version 1.5 signatures. It prefers PSS for new applications, while encouraging a gradual transition from version 1.5 for compatibility.
sections.plainLanguage: OAEP uses published parameter rules to wrap a key for transport. The RFC also lets older version 1.5 signatures use newer hash functions, while recommending PSS for future use.

sections.title: Key Handling and Security Guidance
sections.content:
Implementations must protect RSA private keys and generate key pairs using a suitable random-number generator. The RFC recommends using a key pair for only one scheme and keeping scheme parameters stable for that key, apart from the PSS salt length.

The RFC reports a SHA-1 collision attack and explains that stronger security may require a longer RSA key and a longer hash. Implementations MUST support 1024-bit RSA keys; before the end of 2007, they SHOULD support at least 2048-bit keys and SHA-256. The document requires no IANA action.
sections.plainLanguage: Private keys need protection and sound random generation. The RFC also describes a transition toward longer RSA keys and stronger hashes as security needs increase.
